newsitem.title: USA: AUTOMATIC SEES 15 PCT GROWTH IN FISCAL 1998.
newsitem.headline: AUTOMATIC SEES 15 PCT GROWTH IN FISCAL 1998.

text.p: Automatic Data Processing Inc said Wednesday it expects close to 15 percent growth in revenue and pretax earnings, excluding the non-recurring items recorded in 1997, for fiscal 1998.
Despite a higher anticipated tax rate and increased shares outstanding in 1998, the company said it expects earnings per share growth in the area of 12-14 percent above 1997's $1.80 per share.
The company also said, however, it expects its front office operating results to be cut by $25 million in fiscal year 1998.
Analysts' consensus for earnings per share for the year ending June 30, 1998 is $2.08, according to First Call.
The company said its 1998 forecast includes special re-engineering expenses to cut product lines and consolidate data centers in its brokerage front office business.

The company said its forecast includes "significant" new investments in business expansion, especially in employer services, as well as accelerated investments to support "world class" service and year 2000 compliance.
This re-engineering and the previously announced cancellation of a brokerage front office client contract will lower front office operating results by $25 million in fiscal 1998 versus 1997.
The company reported earnings per share for fiscal 1997 of $1.80 before nonrecurring items, on revenues of $4.11 billion. After nonrecurring items, earnings per share were $1.76.
